title: Homework: moles practice set (12 questions)
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Written for gcse-science/y10 lesson 36 (Complete the moles practice set on the portal (12 questions).)
intro: Moles = mass (g) ÷ Mr; mass = moles × Mr. Use the relative atomic masses: H 1, C 12, O 16, Na 23, Mg 24, S 32, Cl 35.5, Ca 40, Fe 56, Cu 63.5.

questions.q: Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of water, H₂O.
Calculate the Mr of carbon dioxide, CO₂.
Calculate the Mr of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃.
Calculate the Mr of sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄.
How many moles are in 36 g of water?
How many moles are in 22 g of carbon dioxide?
How many moles are in 25 g of calcium carbonate?
Calculate the mass of 3 mol of sodium chloride, NaCl.
Calculate the mass of 0.2 mol of magnesium oxide, MgO.
How many moles are in 4.9 g of sulfuric acid?
Calculate the mass of 0.5 mol of copper sulfate, CuSO₄.
How many moles of atoms are in 112 g of iron?
